lane_proof.convention: Each lane list is most-significant to least-significant (lane3..lane0).
lane_proof.message_arithmetic: Each sum is wrapping u32 addition. cast_signed and cast_unsigned preserve all 32 bits, including the high bit.
lane_proof.first_call: At t=4j, rnds2(cdgh,abef,combined) returns ABEF(t+2) into cdgh. The unchanged old abef equals CDGH(t+2).
lane_proof.second_call: rnds2(old abef,new cdgh,shuffle0x0E(combined)) returns ABEF(t+4) into abef. The saved ABEF(t+2) in cdgh equals CDGH(t+4), restoring the loop invariant.
lane_proof.message_shuffle_meaning: Only low lanes 0 and 1 are consumed, giving W[t+2]+K[t+2] and W[t+3]+K[t+3] in order.
lane_proof.round_count: Two two-round operations for each of exactly 16 four-word chunks = 64 rounds. Both input arrays have length64 and no chunk remainder.
lane_proof.feedforward: The state array is not mutated until the final loop. It receives exactly one wrapping addition of the extracted final working state into the original block state. Early return prevents scalar rounds/feedforward from executing again.
lane_proof.byte_order: Existing from_be_bytes parsing and to_be_bytes digest output are unchanged. Register lane conversion handles integer values, with no host-memory byte reinterpretation.

safety_and_fallback.runtime_precondition: The sole call to target_feature(sha) is dominated by is_x86_feature_detected!("sha").
safety_and_fallback.architecture_scope: The macro import, dispatch block and helper all have cfg(target_arch="x86_64"). Other architectures compile and execute the original scalar code.
safety_and_fallback.unsupported_x86_sha: The runtime guard is false and execution continues through the byte-identical scalar path.
safety_and_fallback.sse2_requirement: Rust Reference lists sha as implicitly enabling sse2. All other used SIMD intrinsics are SSE2; no SSSE3, SSE4, AVX or pointer intrinsic is introduced.
safety_and_fallback.unsafe_block_contents: A call to the guarded target_feature helper only; no raw pointer load/store, pointer cast, transmute or inline assembly.
